exposure: antihypertensive therapy in women with mild-moderate CHTN
outcome: composite perinatal outcomes (fetal growth restriction, intrauterine fetal demise, and small for gestational age neonate)
admission to the neonatal intensive care unit
cohort: 345 singleton pregnancies of women with mild-moderate chronic hypertension who delivered between January 2014 and March 2019
finding: In women with mild-moderate chronic hypertension, the use of antihypertensive therapy prior to 20 weeks gestation did not significantly reduce the risk of developing superimposed preeclampsia with severe features or other adverse maternal or neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: No significant difference in mode of delivery was observed between groups.
